goal.title: Your Goal
goal.subtitle: Choose the purpose that best matches your trip. Categories follow the U.S. Department of State visa directory (travel.state.gov).

citizenship.title: Citizenship & Status
citizenship.subtitle: Some visas (TN, E-3, BCC, H-1B1) depend on nationality or current U.S. status.

employment.title: Employment
employment.subtitle: Most work visas require a U.S. employer petition (USCIS Form I-129 or equivalent) before consular interview.

education.title: Education & Exchange
education.subtitle: Student and exchange visas require SEVIS approval (Form I-20 or DS-2019) before applying.

health.title: Health
health.subtitle: Medical inadmissibility may apply; a civil surgeon exam (Form I-693) is required for immigrant visas.

humanitarian.title: Humanitarian Protection
humanitarian.subtitle: Asylum, U, and T statuses have strict eligibility and often require legal counsel (USCIS / EOIR).

history.title: Visa & Immigration History
history.subtitle: Prior denials, overstays, or deportation can affect eligibility and may trigger entry bars (INA §212).

finance.title: Finances
finance.subtitle: Visitor visas (B-1/B-2) require proof you can fund the trip without unauthorized work (INA §214(b)).

visa_goal.label: What is your main purpose for traveling to the United States?
visa_goal.help: Based on travel.state.gov visa categories. Choose the closest match — you can refine details in later sections.

investment_type.label: What type of investment or trade activity?
investment_type.help: E-1/E-2 require a treaty of commerce with the U.S.; citizenship must be from a treaty country.

eb_immigrant_category.label: Which employment-based immigrant category applies?
eb_immigrant_category.help: Most EB categories require an approved I-140 petition; EB-2/EB-3 usually need PERM labor certification.

dv_lottery_selected.label: Were you selected in the Diversity Visa (DV) lottery for the current fiscal year?
dv_lottery_selected.help: Selection alone does not guarantee a visa — you must still meet education/work requirements and pass interview.

had_permanent_residence.label: Did you previously hold U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card) status?
had_permanent_residence.help: SB-1 returning resident visa is for those who abandoned LPR status and wish to return without a new immigrant petition.

us_citizen_fiance.label: Are you engaged to a U.S. citizen (K-1 fiancé(e) visa)?
us_citizen_fiance.help: K-1 requires an approved I-129F petition; you must marry within 90 days of U.S. entry.

us_citizen_spouse.label: Are you already married to a U.S. citizen (IR/CR immigrant visa)?
us_citizen_spouse.help: Spouses of U.S. citizens apply for IR1/CR1 immigrant visas after an approved I-130 petition.

lpr_family_relationship.label: What is your relationship to the lawful permanent resident?
lpr_family_relationship.help: F2A (spouse/minor child) and F2B (adult unmarried child) have different wait times per Visa Bulletin.

citizenship.label: Country of citizenship (passport issuing country)
citizenship.help: Use the country name as on your passport. Required for TN (Canada/Mexico), E-3 (Australia), BCC (Mexico), H-1B1 (Chile/Singapore).

dual_citizenship.label: Do you hold citizenship of more than one country?

current_us_status.label: Current immigration status in the United States
current_us_status.help: If you are already in the U.S., some applications (adjustment of status, change of status) may be filed with USCIS instead of a consulate.

residence_country.label: Country where you currently live
residence_country.help: You generally apply at the U.S. embassy or consulate in your country of residence.

has_us_job_offer.label: Do you have a written job offer from a U.S. employer?
has_us_job_offer.help: H-1B, L-1, O-1, and most work visas require the employer to file a petition before your visa interview.

job_requires_degree.label: Does the position require at least a bachelor's degree in a specific specialty (H-1B specialty occupation)?

intracompany_transfer.label: Is this an intracompany transfer (L-1) — same employer, foreign office 1+ year?
intracompany_transfer.help: L-1A (manager/executive) or L-1B (specialized knowledge) requires qualifying relationship between entities.

l1_qualifying_employment.label: Have you worked for the foreign affiliate at least 1 continuous year in the last 3 years?
l1_qualifying_employment.help: Required for L-1 eligibility per USCIS — managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge role.

extraordinary_ability.label: Do you have sustained national or international acclaim in your field (O-1)?
extraordinary_ability.help: O-1 requires evidence such as awards, publications, high salary, or leading role in distinguished organizations.

has_university_degree.label: Do you hold a university degree (bachelor's or higher)?
has_university_degree.help: Required for H-1B, E-3, TN (most professions), and many EB categories.

degree_evaluated.label: Have you completed a U.S. credential evaluation (NACES member)?
degree_evaluated.help: Foreign degrees usually need evaluation (WES, ECE, etc.) to show U.S. equivalency.

study_program_type.label: What type of U.S. study or exchange program?

has_i20.label: Do you have a signed Form I-20 from a SEVP-certified school?
has_i20.help: F-1 and M-1 require I-20; pay the I-901 SEVIS fee before your visa interview.

has_ds2019.label: Do you have Form DS-2019 from a designated J-1 program sponsor?
has_ds2019.help: J-1 exchange visitors need DS-2019; some categories have a two-year home residency requirement.

humanitarian_basis.label: Which type of humanitarian protection are you seeking?

life_threat.label: Is your life or freedom threatened in your country of nationality?

persecution.label: Do you fear persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or particular social group?
persecution.help: Protected grounds under INA §101(a)(42)(A) for asylum and withholding of removal.

gender_violence.label: Are you a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, or similar qualifying crime?

crime_victim.label: Were you a victim of a qualifying criminal activity in the U.S.?
crime_victim.help: U visa covers specific crimes listed in INA §101(a)(15)(U)(iii); must have suffered substantial abuse.

crime_victim_cooperation.label: Have you been helpful or likely to be helpful to law enforcement in investigating or prosecuting the crime?
crime_victim_cooperation.help: Certification on Form I-918 Supplement B from a qualifying agency is required for U visa.

trafficking_victim.label: Are you a victim of a severe form of human trafficking?
trafficking_victim.help: T visa requires compliance with reasonable law enforcement requests unless under 18 or traumatized.

deportation_risk.label: Are you currently in removal proceedings or at risk of deportation from the U.S.?

chronic_conditions.label: Do you have chronic health conditions requiring ongoing treatment?
chronic_conditions.help: Certain communicable diseases or conditions without proof of treatment may affect admissibility (INA §212(a)(1)).

disability.label: Do you have a physical or mental disability?
disability.help: Disability alone is not a bar; public charge and medical inadmissibility rules may still apply.

prior_visa_denial.label: Have you ever been refused a U.S. visa or admission at a port of entry?
prior_visa_denial.help: Be prepared to explain what changed since the prior refusal at your interview.

prior_overstay.label: Have you ever remained in the U.S. beyond your authorized stay?
prior_overstay.help: Overstays of 180+ days may trigger 3- or 10-year reentry bars (INA §212(a)(9)(B)).

prior_deportation.label: Have you ever been deported or removed from the United States?
prior_deportation.help: Prior removal may require a waiver (I-212) before reapplying for most visas.

financial_sponsor.label: Who will primarily fund your U.S. stay?

annual_income_usd.label: Your approximate annual income (USD, optional)
annual_income_usd.help: Consular officers assess whether you can afford the trip without unauthorized employment (especially B-1/B-2).

visa_goal.work_has_offer: Work — U.S. employer sponsor (H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN, E-3)
visa_goal.work_seeking_h1b: Work — preparing for H-1B (specialty occupation, no offer yet)
visa_goal.work_seeking: Work — preparing for H-1B (general, no offer yet)
visa_goal.usmca_professional: Work — TN/TD USMCA (Canada or Mexico citizen)
visa_goal.work_seeking_e3: Work — preparing for E-3 (Australian specialty worker)
visa_goal.work_seasonal_ag: Seasonal agricultural work — H-2A (DOL + USCIS petition)
visa_goal.work_seasonal_temp: Temporary non-ag work — H-2B (DOL + USCIS petition)
visa_goal.performing_artist: Performing athlete, artist, entertainer — P visa
visa_goal.family: Family — U.S. citizen fiancé(e) K-1 or spouse IR/CR
visa_goal.adoption: Intercountry adoption — IR3, IH3, IR4, IH4
visa_goal.investment: Treaty trader/investor — E-1 / E-2 (or EB-5 immigrant)
visa_goal.immigrant_employment: Employment-based green card — EB-1 through EB-5
visa_goal.diplomat_official: Diplomat or foreign government official — A visa
visa_goal.border_crossing: Border Crossing Card — Mexico (BCC / laser visa)
visa_goal.humanitarian: Humanitarian protection — Asylum, U, T, or TPS

investment_type.treaty_trader: Substantial trade with the U.S. — E-1 treaty trader
investment_type.treaty_investor: Substantial investment in U.S. business — E-2 treaty investor

eb_immigrant_category.eb1: EB-1 — priority workers (extraordinary ability, outstanding professors, multinational managers)
eb_immigrant_category.eb2: EB-2 — advanced degree or exceptional ability (PERM or NIW)
eb_immigrant_category.eb3: EB-3 — skilled workers, professionals, other workers (PERM required)
eb_immigrant_category.eb5: EB-5 — immigrant investor ($800K+ in targeted area)

humanitarian_basis.asylum: Asylum — fear of persecution in home country
humanitarian_basis.u_visa: U visa — victim of qualifying crime who assisted law enforcement
humanitarian_basis.t_visa: T visa — victim of human trafficking

lpr_family_relationship.adult_child: Unmarried son or daughter 21 or older (F2B)
